title: Customer Exit Chronicle and Salvage Checklist
body:
Purpose
This is a working template for capturing a full customer exit narrative (the "chronicle") and an action-oriented salvage checklist. Use this to power QBRs, renewal retro decks, and internal root-cause workstreams. The emphasis here is on making the timeline, decision points, and plausible counterfactuals explicit so Product, Eng, and CS can quickly operationalize learnings.

Scope / when to use
- Use for any churn (voluntary non-renewal or downgrade) where ARR > $25k or strategic value > medium.
- Use as a quick intake for smaller accounts when time permits.
- This document is intentionally hybrid: robust enough for exec summary + tactical salvage steps for AEs/CSMs.

High-level summary (TL;DR)
- Customer: [COMPANY NAME]
- Contract type: Hosted API (monthly usage) / Dedicated pool / Private (pick one)
- ARR / ARR at risk: [$$$]
- Outcome: Non-renewed as of [date] / Downgrade to X / Contract terminated early
- Primary stated reason: [e.g., Cost, Performance, Feature gap, Legal/compliance, Org change]
- Net win/loss: Why this matters to Redwood (tech stack, public reference, competitive insight)

Owner & stakeholders
- Document owner: [Name] (CSM or Escalation lead)
- AE: [Name]
- Technical AE / Solutions: [Name]
- Eng contact(s): [Name(s)]
- Support triage owner: [Name]

Evidence & signals collected (where we pull data)
- Support tickets / severity timeline (support system IDs)
- Telemetry: latency percentiles, error rates, 95th/99th token latency snapshots (dates/times)
- Billing usage graphs and anomalies (tokens per day, spikes, unexplained drops)
- Console logs / rollout traces (canary timestamps)
- Call/meeting notes, Slack threads, and recorded QBRs
- Win/loss interviews and exit survey responses

Chronological timeline (critical to narrate the moment-by-moment escalation)
- [YYYY-MM-DD] First signal: drop in usage noted by AE; Slack note -> ticket created (TICKET-#)
- [YYYY-MM-DD] Performance incident: 95p latency spikes for 4 hours during batch jobs; customers reported timeouts
- [YYYY-MM-DD] Feature ask escalated: need for deterministic output or structured tool-calls for production integration
- [YYYY-MM-DD] Pricing conversation: customer requests committed discount for predictable unit cost
- [YYYY-MM-DD] Decision: customer pauses pilot; AE escalates to renewal committee
- [YYYY-MM-DD] Renewal declined; customer signs with competitor / moves to internal build

Root-cause analysis (three-layer approach)
1) Immediate technical trigger(s) — facts first
   - e.g., KC-cache eviction pattern under concurrency X caused repeated full recomputation, elevating cost and latency.
   - Attach ticket IDs / trace snippets.
2) Systemic product gaps / limitations
   - e.g., lack of a lightweight deterministic inference mode for short prompts; no out-of-the-box adapter for customer’s toolchain (homegrown vector store).
   - API ergonomics issues: complexity of session/state management for their usage pattern.
3) GTM / account management & pricing mismatch
   - e.g., the packaged offering assumed bursty usage; customer had continuous high-throughput which made hosted pricing unattractive.
   - Failed alignment on runbook ownership between customer SRE and our Solutions team.

Counterfactual scenarios (explicit what-if narratives we might have tried)
- Scenario A — Faster mitigation: If we had launched a canary of dedup/caching fix within 48 hours, and flagged the customer for premium remediation, probability of retention: medium-high. Key actions: emergency patch, credited tokens, SLA modification, daily standups.
- Scenario B — Different commercial offer: If we had offered a time-limited committed capacity discount + dedicated pool trial for 90 days, probability: medium. Key actions: draft contract addendum, finance approval, ops capacity reservation.
- Scenario C — Product workaround + integration: If Solutions had shipped a reference adapter for the customer's vector store + pattern doc within 2 weeks, probability: low-medium but would reduce engineering churn.
- For each scenario, capture (i) timeline to execute, (ii) owner, (iii) blockers, (iv) cost to Redwood (ops + credits + engineering time).

Decision matrix (quick assessment)
- Likelihood vs Impact table (fill in): High/Med/Low for each counterfactual. Use this to recommend whether to pursue future accounts with same profile, invest in product fix, or update pricing.

Salvage checklist (immediate / near-term actions)
- Immediate (0–7 days):
  - Convene cross-functional triage (CSM, AE, Solutions, Eng on-call, Finance).
  - Pull and freeze all relevant telemetry and logs; snapshot for postmortem archive.
  - Prepare customer-facing acknowledgement email (empathy + timeline for next steps).
  - Issue goodwill credits where justified and track in finance ticket.
- Near-term (7–30 days):
  - Implement or schedule temporary workarounds (caching rules, rate-limits, configuration templates).
  - Draft a commercial counteroffer (term-limited trial of Dedicated / reserved pool, or custom discount).
  - Ship a playbook snippet for CSMs describing the exact config parameters that helped similar accounts.
- Long-term (>30 days):
  - Product backlog item(s) for deterministic mode / integration adapter.
  - Consider a whitepaper or engineering-runbook for customers with continuous high-throughput patterns.
  - Update pricing packaging for high-constant-throughput customers.

Postmortem artifacts to produce (owner + due dates)
- Technical postmortem (Eng): include traces and root-cause analysis — owner: [name], due: +14 days
- Commercial retrospective (CS + Sales): summary of negotiations and counteroffer decisions — owner: [name], due: +10 days
- QBR slide pack for execs (one slide summary + top 3 recommendations) — owner: [name], due: +7 days

QBR inputs and talking points (for Customer Success leader)
- One-slide TL;DR (Outcome, Primary root cause, Recommended next steps)
- Financial impact: ARR lost, churn delta versus cohort, forecast adjustment
- Product ask: prioritized fixes and estimated TTM
- Field learnings: how many other accounts fit this risk profile?

Checklist for lessons & follow-ups
- Are there 3+ similar customers at risk? If yes -> trigger Product/Packaging review.
- Did we log a clear decision rule for future similar cases? (e.g., auto-offer dedicated pool for usage > X tokens/day)
- Did Finance approve salvage credits and were they tracked against renewal?
- Did we document a repeatable integration pattern for Solutions?

Unresolved questions / notes to self
- Was the initial latency spike correlated with a model rollout? (Investigate rollout tags)
- Could a deterministic inference option materially reduce egress cost for this workload?
- Identify the CSM handoff point that failed (timeline of last proactive check-in vs. signal).

Appendix: quick templates
- Customer-facing acknowledgement (short):
  - "Thanks for flagging this. We take performance and cost very seriously. We're assembling a cross-functional team and will follow up with a remediation plan within 48 hours. In the meantime, we have frozen token billing for the impacted window and will propose credits if the root cause is on our side."
- Example commercial clause (internal draft):
  - "90-day Dedicated trial with X reserved units; if performance targets met, convert to 12-month commitment at Y discount. Finance approval required."

References & links
- Attach ticket list, telemetry snapshots, call recordings, and the AE’s renewal notes.
- Link to related Confluence playbooks: "High-throughput pricing playbook", "Dedup cache runbook"

How to file this doc when complete
- Mark status -> final after all postmortem artifacts are attached and owners have signed off.
- Move a copy to: shared_drives/retros/2025/q4/ (or archived path) and tag with churn cohort.

Notes on tone & usage
- Keep this file a single source of truth for the account's exit story. Write plainly, cite tickets and timestamps, and make counterfactuals explicit and actionable.
- This document is intentionally a hybrid: it should be used in QBR decks, but also be granular enough for Eng and Finance to act on immediate remediation and credit decisions.

Draft notes (internal)
- Still need: exact billing snapshot for Oct 2025; transcript from renewal call; engineering trace for 2025-10-12 03:00 UTC.
- Next step owner: Priya Shah (this doc), coordinate with Ethan Park to get trace snapshots.

-- end of template --
